title: Apache Spark vs VecRuntime vs DataFusion Comet on TPC-DS 1 TB
dataset: TPC-DS scale factor 1000 (1 TB), Parquet on Amazon S3 (103 query variants, one measured iteration each, no warm-up)
cluster: Amazon EKS 1.36; 9 x m5.4xlarge (16 vCPU, 64 GB, x86-64 with AVX-512), 300 GB root volume; one node group in one availability zone (us-east-1a), the driver on the ninth node
executors: 8 executors x 13 cores x 50 GB each (Spark: 20 GB heap / 30 GB overhead; VecRuntime: 30 GB heap / 20 GB overhead; Comet: 20 GB heap / 8 GB overhead / 22 GB off-heap; Comet Native Scan + VecRuntime: 30 GB heap / 12 GB overhead / 8 GB off-heap); driver 2 cores x 4 GB
storage: Amazon S3 through an S3 gateway VPC endpoint, Hadoop 3.4.3 S3A with the Analytics Accelerator input stream (the default in 3.4.3); fs.s3a.connection.maximum=1000, threads.max=256, max.total.tasks=128, Analytics Accelerator physicalio.thread.pool.size=192 for every engine (#566)

versions.JDK: Amazon Corretto 25, -XX:+UseCompactObjectHeaders and Amazon Corretto Crypto Provider on driver and executors (#578, #566)
versions.VecRuntime: main at bbc7261 (#579 native Parquet reader with read-ahead, #580, #581)

common_conf: # spark.sql.adaptive.advisoryPartitionSizeInBytes left at Spark's default (64 MB); no coalescePartitions.minPartitionNum
vector_conf: spark.vecruntime.scan.nativeParquet.prefetchFiles=6   # default: files read ahead per split
spark.vecruntime.scan.nativeParquet.prefetchRowGroups=2   # default: row groups read ahead per file
spark.vecruntime.shuffle.aqe.mapSizeScaling=true   # AQE sees Spark-scale map output sizes (#514)
mixed_conf: spark.comet.scan.enabled=true   # CometNativeScanExec: DataFusion's Rust Parquet reader and object_store S3 I/O
spark.comet.exec.enabled=true   # with every Comet operator switched off: filter, project, aggregate, joins, sort, window, ...
spark.memory.offHeap.size=8g   # executors 30 GB heap / 12 GB overhead / 8 GB off-heap
notes: Every engine returned Spark's row counts on every query, and Spark's checksums on every query except q65, whose result has ties that every engine orders differently.

The four legs ran on 2026-10-02 in one cluster session on the same nine nodes, one after another (Spark, VecRuntime, Comet Native Scan + VecRuntime, Comet), each alone on the cluster. S3 throughput varies between sessions, so only legs from one session are compared.

VecRuntime runs on its own Parquet reader here (spark.vecruntime.scan.nativeParquet.enabled=true, #559): pages decoded in Java straight into the Arrow buffers its operators read, with the next files and row groups of each split read ahead on background threads. The flag is off by default; the earlier runs on this page (docs/results.md) used Spark's reader.
Comet is the 1.0.0 release from Maven Central. The S3A settings, ACCP and compact object headers are the benchmark launcher's defaults since #566 and #578 and apply to all four engines.
AQE is at its defaults for every engine.
methodology_html: Methodology. Spark, VecRuntime, Comet Native Scan + VecRuntime and Comet ran one after another in one cluster session on 2026-10-02, on the same nine nodes, each alone on the cluster, over the same S3 data with the same Spark settings; only the execution engine and its own memory split differ (every engine has 50 GB per executor; where it puts them follows where it allocates). Each query ran once after the plan was compiled; the time is the wall-clock of the query's execution as the runner measures it.
wins_html: The scan-bound queries are now VecRuntime's, on its own Parquet reader: q88 35.0 s against Spark's 96.1 and Comet's 84.2; q9 30.6 against 73.2 and 50.5; q28 58.4 against 101.8 and 67.3; q44 9.6 against 34.8 and 22.0; q90 7.4 against 30.7 and 31.0. So are the heavy joins: q23b 104.0 against 288.2 and 138.1; q64 25.5 against 87.6 and 48.8; q93 51.9 against 129.2 and 72.2. Comet Native Scan + VecRuntime (the same operators on Comet's Rust reader) finishes in 1,954 s against VecRuntime's 1,542 s on its own reader, so the reader is now the faster one of the two. Comet leads on the heavy aggregates and a few mid-size queries: q4 57.1 against VecRuntime's 70.6, q11 30.5 against 38.6, q24a 79.2 against 93.7, q24b 74.8 against 90.9, q65 13.1 against 19.0, q18 4.5 against 12.1. VecRuntime's losses to Spark are q18 (12.1 s against 8.0, under investigation), q99 (10.0 against 8.4), q92 (1.9 against 1.6) and q12 (2.3 against 2.2).
vector_vs_comet: and leads on the scan-bound queries and the heavy joins; Comet leads on the heavy aggregates (q4, q11, q24a/b, q67) and q18
results_line: Every engine returned Spark's results (q65: ties, ordered differently by every engine).
mixed_line: Same operators and shuffle as VecRuntime, on Comet's Rust Parquet reader.
